title: The Cloud-Text Where Meaning Falls

features.name: reading-clouds
features.desc-on-touch: Text descends from above. You read what falls. Before you finish reading, you've forgotten what it said, and you read it again for the first time.

features.name: descent-cascade
features.desc-on-touch: Meaning falls in drops. Each drop carries a story. The stories pool at your feet and begin to argue.

features.name: cloud-forms
features.desc-on-touch: Vapour that remembers the shape of every letter it once held, still holding them.

features.name: measurement-device
features.desc-on-touch: A rusted rain-gauge. The numbers on it change depending on what language you read them in.

features.name: sky-archive
features.desc-on-touch: Letters written in cumulus. The archive of all things the sky has learned to say.

inscription: the sky's own alphabetizing, falling as weather

file.name: CloudTranscript_July_1987_Complete_Recording.mp3
file.note: Seven hours of rain-text. The archive recorded what the clouds spelled. Each time you listen, you hear different words arriving. The clouds are still composing.

reverie.title: REVERIE — teaching language to the rain
narr: Katita stands with you in the falling rain, teaching you to read
what the sky is writing. "Listen," she says. "See? That drop—"
She points. "That's a word in three languages at once, until the
ground forgets how many tongues it heard." Rain collects in your
palms. By the time you look up, the clouds have rewritten
everything. "Again," she smiles. "Let's read it again from start."
